skill.summary: Research Xiaohongshu topics, posts, comments, and creators through SocialDataX read-only commands.

security_audit.summary: All 59 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, documented service configuration, platform identifiers, or readable Chinese text. Two semantic risks remain: automatic execution of an unpinned npm package and mandatory disclosure of token-bearing note URLs. No evidence found of malicious payloads, credential theft, or audit-directed prompt injection in the reviewed files; external package behavior was not inspected.

remediation.issue: Examples automatically execute the mutable socialdatax-skills@latest package with installation prompts suppressed.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and verify package integrity before execution. Request installation consent and restrict credentials available to the process.

remediation.issue: Output instructions require retaining xsec_token in displayed, stored, and forwarded note URLs without a sensitivity check.
remediation.suggestion: Treat token-bearing URLs as potentially sensitive. Retain complete URLs only for authorized retrieval, and use note IDs in shared outputs by default.

semantic_findings.description: Examples use npx -y socialdatax-skills@latest to retrieve and execute a mutable external package. Unreviewed updates could execute with the user's permissions and service credential.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Every CLI example uses @latest and -y, while runtime authentication requires an environment credential. The trust exposure is explicit; no evidence found of package compromise.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory Disclosure of Token-Bearing Note URLs

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly requires token inclusion across output destinations without a sensitivity check. The files do not establish the token's privileges or lifetime.

content.user_title: Research Xiaohongshu Content and Audience Feedback
content.value_statement: Content teams need evidence about topics, audience feedback, and creator activity before planning posts. This skill organizes SocialDataX retrieval workflows into focused Xiaohongshu research.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve current Xiaohongshu hot-search rankings and available popularity signals through SocialDataX.
Search posts by keyword and apply supported sorting, post type, and publication time filters.
Retrieve post details by content ID, URL, or share text.
Collect comments and reply threads, with pagination and partial-result recovery guidance.
Retrieve creator profiles and posted-note lists using account IDs or profile links.
Organize visible evidence into topic patterns, audience reactions, content angles, and creator positioning.
limitations: Live retrieval requires a SocialDataX API key, network access, available service credits, and a working CLI or configured MCP tools.
The supplied files contain instructions and tool mappings, not the external CLI implementation or an independent dataset.
Results may be partial, rate limited, or unavailable; sampled posts do not establish platform-wide trends.
The workflow is read-only and does not log in, publish posts, like content, submit comments, or modify accounts.

use_cases.title: Plan Evidence-Based Content Topics
use_cases.description: Compare hot-search signals and keyword samples to identify content angles, supporting examples, and unanswered audience questions.

use_cases.title: Review Competitor Audience Feedback
use_cases.description: Inspect relevant posts and comment threads to distinguish recurring product questions from isolated reactions.

use_cases.title: Study Creator Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare creator profile information with recent post evidence before choosing a content direction.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Xiaohongshu for [topic] using one page of results. Summarize relevant titles, authors, and three content angles. Separate observations from interpretations.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Post and Its Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve details and one page of comments for [note ID or URL]. Summarize visible audience questions and recurring themes. State any missing data.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Creator Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [creator A] and [creator B] using their profiles and one page of posts each. Compare positioning, recurring topics, and available engagement signals. Cite evidence separately from judgments.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Bounded Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic] for [audience] using hot-search signals, keyword results, and selected comments. Limit retrieval to [page limit] pages and [item limit] items. Preserve partial results and continue only within those limits. Report evidence, uncertainty, and proposed content angles. Do not expose credentials or sensitive URL tokens in shared outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: a multi-source brief with explicit retrieval limits

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Plan topics from a one-page search for small apartment storage.
output: Illustrative format only; no live platform data was retrieved.
Observed evidence: List returned titles, authors, available engagement signals, and note IDs.
Topic patterns: Group the sampled posts by storage location and audience question.
Proposed angles: Explain which visible examples support each suggested topic.
Limit: One page is a sample, not evidence of platform-wide demand.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Summarize audience questions from a selected post and its replies.
output: Illustrative format only; no comments were retrieved.
Post facts: Record the returned author, publication time, and available engagement metrics.
Comment themes: Group visible questions and cite supporting comment evidence.
Coverage: State whether replies are complete, partial, or not yet expanded.
Next step: Continue only with the matching returned token and remaining retrieval allowance.

best_practices: Start with one page and explicit item limits; preserve partial results before requesting more data.
Keep observations separate from interpretations, and state sample size and coverage gaps.
Use a reviewed, pinned CLI version and keep API keys and potentially sensitive URL tokens out of shared reports.
anti_patterns: Treating a small post sample or hot-search ranking as proof of platform-wide audience demand.
Restarting retrieval after partial failures without checking continuation tokens and remaining limits.
Executing unreviewed package updates or forwarding token-bearing URLs without checking authorization.

faq.question: What inputs can I provide?
faq.answer: Provide keywords, a research topic, post links or IDs, creator profile links, account share text, or platform account IDs.

faq.question: Do I need a SocialDataX API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY through your environment. Obtain or manage the key through the declared SocialDataX website.

faq.question: Does this skill publish or interact with posts?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow retrieves information and does not log in, post, like, comment, or change accounts.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Live retrieval still requires usable CLI execution or the documented MCP tools.

faq.question: What happens when results are incomplete?
faq.answer: Keep retrieved items and report the error. Continue with the matching returned token only when limits allow; do not automatically restart.

faq.question: Are there costs or installation concerns?
faq.answer: Service credits may be required. CLI examples use an unpinned npm package; review and pin it before execution.
